counterexamples.evidence: On render_decision.finalMovestring 333222336212244151100550446 visualize_board lists TWO X major threats, 'col7 row3 (X) [GT]' and 'col7 row4 (X)'. c7r4 completes the diagonal c4r1(X move1)·c5r2(X move15)·c6r3(X move23)·c7r4 — that is the second prong that makes c7r2 a fork. forkWindows contains only [[c4r3,c5r3,c6r3,c7r3]] and the assembled prompt exposes c7r4 only as 'major at c7r4 (you)', with no zone alias. Runs 1 and 2 both reached for that second prong ('the key diagonal path', 'both winning ideas at once') and had nothing to wrap it in.

Run 2's raw output emits you-key-line, you-future-fork, played-col and better-col but omits you-fork-pivot, so the served text names the fork square c7r3 and never the square that CREATES the fork (c7r2, X move 27 on 333222336212244151100550446). The handle was offered AND required in the prompt (line 102), so this is prompt_confusion, not missing_info; production's required-set retry would have fired here (OI-183: unexercised in this harness).

PROMPT.includes('column 7') === true ('The book move is column 7'; 'Column 7 was the move that kept it'), yet run 0's mechanism names only 'the book line' and 'column 2'. Information was present and unambiguous — model drop, not render suppression.
